title: 欧洲央行若走得更远：之后将不得不降息，完全没被定价？
speaker: Luigi Speranza

segments.en: And what about, you know, other DM markets, right?
segments.zh: 那么其他发达市场呢，对吧？

segments.en: I mean, the BOJ comes up next after the Fed. That's almost like near guarantee that they're going to hike this week as well.
segments.zh: 我的意思是，日本央行在美联储之后。几乎可以保证他们本周也会加息。

segments.en: You also have the ECB that just hiked rates, BOE. How is pricing look to you on those key markets now?
segments.zh: 还有刚刚加息的欧洲央行、英国央行。你现在怎么看这些关键市场的定价？

segments.en: So the bank of Japan, I think, will increase rates. And the message should be reasonably oakish here, suggesting an acceleration in the pace of rate hike.
segments.zh: 所以日本央行，我认为会加息。信息应该相当鹰派，暗示加息步伐加快。

segments.en: So one for each quarter. Until we get to 175, I guess that to be a good point for the bank of Japan to take a pose.
segments.zh: 所以每季度一次。直到达到1.75%，我猜那会是日本央行暂停的好时机。

segments.en: But we expect them then to resume rate hike later in the year for a terminal rate of around 250.
segments.zh: 但我们预计他们会在今年晚些时候恢复加息，终端利率在2.50%左右。

segments.en: ECB as well, actually on the ECB, we are probably the markets, I think, a bit to some wine about the ECB. I do expect another one in December.
segments.zh: 欧洲央行也是，实际上关于欧洲央行，我们可能，我认为市场对欧洲央行有点过于悲观。我确实预计十二月还有一次。

segments.en: But once you reach the 30 territory and the kind of the neutral rate range, the probably the top is 250, then I think the ECB is going to be a bit more cautious about further rate hike.
segments.zh: 但一旦达到3%区域和中性利率范围，顶部可能是2.50%，那么我认为欧洲央行对进一步加息会更加谨慎。

segments.en: The markets are rising. Our base case is for them to stop at 25.
segments.zh: 市场在上升。我们的基准判断是他们会在2.5%停止。

segments.en: If they go further, I would think they will have to cut rates at later stage. And that's not price at all.
segments.zh: 如果他们走得更远，我认为他们之后将不得不降息。而这完全没有被定价。

segments.en: So I'll be probably be more dovish from the ECB perspective.
segments.zh: 所以从欧洲央行的角度看，我可能会更偏鸽派。

segments.en: There is a key difference here between the ECB and other central banks like Bank of Japan and the Fed.
segments.zh: 欧洲央行与日本央行和美联储等其他央行之间存在关键差异。

segments.en: Inflation is merely an energy issue at this stage. So it's a negative supply shock for the economy.
segments.zh: 目前通胀仅仅是能源问题。所以对经济来说是负面的供给冲击。

segments.en: While for Japan, for the Fed, it's much more domestically generated in change that is why it's probably a bit more action.
segments.zh: 而对日本、对美联储来说，通胀更多是国内产生的变化，这就是为什么可能需要更多行动。

segments.en: With all these hikes priced, and if they do proceed with raising interest rates, just about across the world, how does growth look to you this time next year?
segments.zh: 在所有这些加息被定价的情况下，如果他们确实继续在全球范围内加息，明年此时增长在你看来如何？
